findings.rationale: Feature distribution jumps abruptly at round 11 (shift_sd about 1.0 on HighBP/DiffWalk/GenHlth, versus about 0.03 at round 10), and the shift persists through round 20. The client's update direction also flips at round 11: cosine to the median update falls from about 0.80 to about -0.09 and stays negative, with the norm ratio rising to about 2.9. The local AUC and CITL are not anomalous, so this looks like data drift that trains the client away from the federation rather than poisoning. Whole-federation drift summary: WA mean_shift_sd z=+7.9.

Abrupt feature shift at round 11 (DiffWalk, then HighBP and GenHlth), with shift_sd of about 0.8 to 1.3 in every round from 11 to 20, against about 0.0 to 0.14 before. The client's updates also turn against the median (min cos -0.77, flagged min_cos z=-4.5). Its subgroup O/E for Sex group 1.0 is elevated (1.451, z_noise 6.2), consistent with a shifted population. Local AUC is normal. Whole-federation drift summary: CA mean_shift_sd z=+4.0 with onset_round 11.

Feature shift turns on at round 11 (GenHlth, then HighBP and DiffWalk), with shift_sd of about 0.7 to 1.4 in every round from 11 to 20, against about 0.0 to 0.27 before. Its updates show the same sign flip (min cos -0.63, min_cos z=-3.8). Its subgroup O/E is elevated in both Sex groups (group 1.0: 1.352, group 0.0 FNR z=3.6). Local AUC is normal. Whole-federation drift summary: CO mean_shift_sd z=+3.9 and max_shift_sd z=+3.4, onset_round 11.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex and AgeGroup), then confirmed suspects with per-client drift and update queries. Three clients (WA, CA, CO) show the same pattern: an abrupt feature-distribution shift starting at round 11 that persists, a sign flip in their updates from that round, and elevated subgroup O/E, while their local AUC stays normal. I classify these as drift with onset round 11. Unconfirmed leads that I did not report because the evidence is weak or from small clients: GU (mean_cos z=-3.4, Sex group 1.0 O/E z_noise 4.4), ND (HighChol sd z_noise 5.9), NC (GenHlth p99 z_noise -5.8), and small-client AgeGroup outliers (WI, DC). The attribution-churn screen (explanation_instability) was not run, because the budget was spent on the screens and confirmations; no client showed the large-norm, low-cosine signature of random upload noise in client_updates. The full budget (20.0) is spent.
